But now you have stirred me up; I should like extremely to see some Druids’ stones. arxiv-2102-06551.title: A Little Pretraining Goes a Long Way: A Case Study on Dependency Parsing Task for Low-resource Morphologically Rich Languages
arxiv-2102-06551.creator: Jivnesh Sandhan 1, Amrith Krishna 2, Ashim Gupta 3
arxiv-2102-06551.description: Abstract Neural dependency parsing has achieved remarkable performance for many domains and languages. The bottleneck of massive labeled data limits the effectiveness of these approaches for low resource languages. In this work, we focus on dependency parsing for morphological rich languages (MRLs) in a low-resource setting.

arxiv-2206-08767.title: Testing chiral unitary models for the Λ ⁡ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) in K + ​ π ​ Σ K^{+}\pi\Sigma photoproduction
arxiv-2206-08767.creator: P. C. Bruns, A. Cieplý, M. Mai
arxiv-2206-08767.description: Abstract We adopt a novel formalism for the low-energy analysis of the γ ​ p → K + ​ π ​ Σ \gamma p\to K^{+}\pi\Sigma photoproduction reaction to calculate the π ​ Σ \pi\Sigma invariant mass distributions in the Λ ⁡ ( 1405 ) \Lambda(1405) resonance region.

arxiv-2209-04290.title: Conformance Checking for Trace Fragments Using Infix and Postfix Alignments
arxiv-2209-04290.creator: Daniel Schuster, Niklas Föcking, Sebastiaan J. van Zelst, Wil M. P. van der Aalst
arxiv-2209-04290.description: Abstract Conformance checking deals with collating modeled process behavior with observed process behavior recorded in event data. Alignments are a state-of-the-art technique to detect, localize, and quantify deviations in process executions, i.e., traces, compared to reference process models. Alignments, however, assume complete process executions covering the entire process from start to finish or prefixes of process executions.

arxiv-2212-04540.title: TinyKG: Memory-Efficient Training Framework for Knowledge Graph Neural Recommender Systems Conference: Sixteenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems; September 18–23, 2022; Seattle, WA, USA Sixteenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys ’22), September 18–23, 2022, Seattle, WA, USA Price:
arxiv-2212-04540.creator: Huiyuan Chen, Xiaoting Li, Kaixiong Zhou, Xia Hu, Chin-Chia Michael Yeh, Yan Zheng, Hao Yang
arxiv-2212-04540.description: Abstract . There has been an explosion of interest in designing various Knowledge Graph Neural Networks (KGNNs), which achieve state-of-the-art performance and provide great explainability for recommendation. The promising performance is mainly resulting from their capability of capturing high-order proximity messages over the knowledge graphs. However, training KGNNs at scale is challenging due to the high memory usage.

arxiv-2302-09512.title: SAT Requires Exhaustive Search
arxiv-2302-09512.creator: Guangyan Zhou
arxiv-2302-09512.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Guangyan Zhou. In this paper, by constructing extremely hard examples of CSP (with large domains) and SAT (with long clauses), we prove that such examples cannot be solved without exhaustive search, which is stronger than P ≠ \neq NP. This constructive approach for proving impossibility results is very different (and missing) from those currently used in computational complexity theory, but is similar to that used by Kurt Gödel in proving his famous logical impossibility results.

arxiv-2305-00017.title: Discovering the Origin of Neutrino Masses at SHiP
arxiv-2305-00017.creator: Seyda Ipek, Douglas Tuckler
arxiv-2305-00017.description: Abstract In U ​ ( 1 ) R U(1)_{R} extensions of supersymmetric models, the bino and its Dirac partner, the singlino, can play the role of right-handed neutrinos. The bino and the singlino form a pseudo-dirac pair, dubbed the ‘bi ν \nu o’, which can generate Standard Model neutrino masses via the inverse seesaw mechanism.

arxiv-2308-16279.title: Classification of Anomalies in Telecommunication Network KPI Time Series
arxiv-2308-16279.creator: Korantin Bordeau–Aubert 1 , Justin Whatley 2 , Sylvain Nadeau 2 , Tristan Glatard 1 , Brigitte Jaumard 1
arxiv-2308-16279.description: Abstract The increasing complexity and scale of telecommunication networks have led to a growing interest in automated anomaly detection systems. However, the classification of anomalies detected on network Key Performance Indicators (KPI) has received less attention, resulting in a lack of information about anomaly characteristics and classification processes. To address this gap, this paper proposes a modular anomaly classification framework.

arxiv-2402-16551.title: Delayed-feedback oscillators replicate the dynamics of multiplex networks: wavefront propagation and stochastic resonance
arxiv-2402-16551.creator: Anna Zakharova cor1, Vladimir V. Semenov cor2
arxiv-2402-16551.description: Abstract The widespread development and use of neural networks have significantly enriched a wide range of computer algorithms and promise higher speed at lower cost. However, the imitation of neural networks by means of modern computing substrates is highly inefficient, whereas physical realization of large scale networks remains challenging.

arxiv-2404-02329.title: The Least Prime in Arithmetic an Progression Thanks: Andrew Fiori acknowledges the support of NSERC Discovery Grant RGPIN-2020-05316. Thanks: The computations for this work were conducted on systems supported by the University of Lethbridge and purchased through an NSERC RTI grant.
arxiv-2404-02329.creator: Andrew Fiori
arxiv-2404-02329.description: Abstract . In his 1979 paper Samuel Wagstaff studied the problem of bounding the first prime in an arithmetic progression. In this paper we update a number of his computations using advances in hardware. Based on this we refine his conjecture on Primes in Arithmetic Progression and provide further numerical evidence in support of it.

arxiv-2504-00128.title: Improving Predictions of Convective Storm Wind Gusts through Statistical Post-Processing of Neural Weather Models
arxiv-2504-00128.creator: Antoine Leclerc, Erwan Koch, Monika Feldmann, Daniele Nerini, Tom Beucler
arxiv-2504-00128.description: Abstract Issuing timely severe weather warnings helps mitigate potentially disastrous consequences. Recent advancements in Neural Weather Models (NWMs) offer a computationally inexpensive and fast approach for forecasting atmospheric environments on a 0.25 ∘ global grid. For thunderstorms, these environments can be empirically post-processed to predict wind gust distributions at specific locations.

arxiv-2509-11189.title: Deterministic coherence and anti-coherence resonances in two coupled Lorenz oscillators: numerical study versus experiment
arxiv-2509-11189.creator: Pavel S. Komkov, Ol’ga I. Moskalenko, Vladimir V. Semenov, Sergei V. Grishin
arxiv-2509-11189.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pavel S. Komkov, Ol’ga I. Moskalenko, Vladimir V. Semenov, Sergei V. Grishin. We demonstrate the deterministic coherence and anti-coherence resonance phenomena in two coupled identical chaotic Lorenz oscillators. Both effects are found to occur simultaneously when varying the coupling strength.

arxiv-2601-02551.title: Using 23 Years of ACS/SBC Data to Understand Backgrounds : Significant Reductions in Expected Background Levels
arxiv-2601-02551.creator: Christopher. J. R. Clark, Roberto J. Avila, Alyssa Guzman, Norman A. Grogin
arxiv-2601-02551.description: Abstract We have used 23 years of ACS/SBC data to study what background levels are encountered in practice and how much they vary. The backgrounds vary considerably, with F115LP, F122M, F125LP, PR110L, and PR130L all showing over an order of magnitude of variation in background between observations, apparently due to changes in airglow.

pmc-13112799.description: An 8-year, 10-month-old female spayed British Shorthair cat was referred for progressive tetraparesis. At presentation, the cat was non-ambulatory with left-sided hemiparesis Cervical magnetic resonance imaging showed presence of extradural disc material causing moderate spinal cord compression at C3-C4 and C4-C5 levels, and mild compression at C5-C6 level.

pmc-13383896.title: Combined Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction With Bone‐Patellar Tendon‐Bone Autograft and Anatomical Lateral Collateral Ligament and Proximal Tibiofibular Joint Reconstruction Using Semitendinosus Allograft
pmc-13383896.creator: Ryan J. Froom, Alexi J. Panos, Nate J. Dickinson, Molly E. Kessenich, Matthew T. Provencher
pmc-13383896.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Multiligamentous knee injuries involving anterior cruciate ligament rupture and lateral‐sided instability, including proximal tibiofibular joint instability and lateral collateral ligament deficiency, present unique challenges in restoring knee stability. This Technical Note describes a reproducible surgical technique for anatomic reconstruction of the anterior cruciate ligament using a bone‐patellar tendon‐bone autograft and combined lateral collateral ligament and proximal tibiofibular joint reconstruction using a single semitendinosus allograft.

pmc-13588095.title: Initial magnetic resonance imaging/magnetic resonance angiography may miss intracranial artery dissection in young adults with stroke: the role of subsequent imaging
pmc-13588095.creator: Naoki Makita, Tomoyuki Ohara, Masahiro Makino, Eijirou Tanaka, Daiki Fukunaga, Naoki Tokuda, Akihiro Fujii, Hidesato Takezawa, Keisuke Imai, Takehiro Yamada, Yoshinari Nagakane, Shiori Ogura, Keiko Maezono-Kandori, Toshiki Mizuno
pmc-13588095.description: IntroductionIntracranial artery dissection (IAD) is an important cause of ischaemic stroke in young adults; however, its diagnosis at initial presentation remains challenging. We aimed to determine how often initial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)/magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) and subsequent imaging identified IAD, and to clarify the timing of IAD diagnosis.
